```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  fold = TRUE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 7,
  dpi = 150
)
# Fold every chunk's code under a "Code" toggle. pkgdown ignores
# `code_folding: hide`, so the toggle is a <details> block around the source.
src_hook <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("source")
knitr::knit_hooks$set(source = function(x, options) {
  out <- src_hook(x, options)
  if (!isTRUE(options$fold)) return(out)
  paste0("\n<details><summary>Code</summary>\n\n", paste(out, collapse = "\n"),
         "\n\n</details>\n")
})
# The fetch code is shown from the data-raw script, so what is shown is what ran:
# from_script("label") is the block between "## ---- label" and the next "## ----".
script <- readLines(file.path("..", "..", "data-raw", "floodplain_change_dating.R"))
from_script <- function(label) {
  marks <- grep("^## ----", script)
  i <- match(paste("## ----", label), script)
  if (is.na(i)) stop("No block '", label, "' in the data-raw script")
  end <- marks[marks > i][1] - 1
  script[(i + 1):end]
}
```


```{r data, include = FALSE}
# The figures read the files data-raw/floodplain_change_dating.R saved;
# nothing here goes to the network. s2_view is
# the composites as 8-bit display bytes on one stretch, and change.tif holds a
# clean switch's year less 2000.
library(terra)
d <- function(f) file.path("floodplain-change-dating", f)
crs <- "EPSG:32609"

item <- utils::read.csv(d("item.csv"))
summ <- utils::read.csv(d("summary.csv"))
areas <- utils::read.csv(d("areas.csv"), na.strings = "")
caps <- utils::read.csv(d("captures.csv"))
caps$capture_date <- as.Date(caps$capture_date)
sharp <- caps[caps$res_m < 1, ]
newest <- max(sharp$capture_date)
newest_first <- as.Date(sharp$release_first[sharp$capture_date == newest])
newest_last <- as.Date(sharp$release_last[sharp$capture_date == newest])
fmt <- function(x) format(as.Date(x), "%Y-%m-%d")
yr <- function(x) format(as.Date(x), "%Y")

change <- rast(d("change.tif"))
box_km <- round(c(xmax(change) - xmin(change), ymax(change) - ymin(change)) / 1000, 1)
asp <- (ymax(change) - ymin(change)) / (xmax(change) - xmin(change))
years <- 2017:2023
s2_view <- setNames(lapply(years, function(y) rast(d(paste0("s2_", y, ".tif")))), years)

fpc <- utils::read.csv(d("floodplain.csv"))
fp_edge <- vect(fpc$wkt[fpc$part == "edge"], crs = crs)
area_v <- vect(areas$wkt, crs = crs)
relief <- rast(d("relief_bulk.tif"))
relief_credit <- readLines(d("relief_credit.txt"))
ctx <- utils::read.csv(d("context.csv"))
ctx_v <- function(part) vect(ctx$wkt[ctx$part == part], crs = ctx$crs[ctx$part == part][1])
# ground outside the floodplain is dimmed, so the floodplain reads as the subject
outside <- ifel(is.na(change), 1, NA)

# What the imagery shows in each area was read off the panels below. It is tied
# to the areas it was read for, so a rerun that changes them stops the build
# rather than putting a verdict on the wrong area.
seen_by_eye <- data.frame(
  key = c("A 2018 Crops Rangeland", "B 2018 Rangeland Trees", "C 2019 Trees Rangeland",
          "D 2020 Crops Rangeland", "E 2020 Crops Rangeland", "F 2021 Trees Rangeland",
          "G 2022 Trees Rangeland", "H 2022 Trees Crops", "I 2023 Trees Rangeland",
          "J 2023 Trees Rangeland"),
  shows = c("Part of one open meadow; its western arm crosses the strip mown in 2016",
            "The same stand of trees before and after",
            "Creekside forest opened up",
            "Part of the same meadow; mown in 2016, grassed in 2020",
            "Part of the same meadow, running into a farmyard; its southern lobe crosses the strip mown in 2016",
            "Forest in 2020, then brightens in 2021",
            "An open wet meadow along a channel in 2020, then brightens over 2021 and 2022",
            "Forest in 2020, then brightens in 2022",
            "Forest in 2020, then opens up in 2023",
            "Forest in 2020, then opens up in 2023"),
  ground = c("Class error", "Class error", "Change", "Class error", "Class error",
             "Likely change", "Unclear", "Likely change", "Likely change", "Likely change")
)
if (!identical(paste(areas$id, areas$year, areas$from, areas$to), seen_by_eye$key)) {
  stop("areas.csv has changed: look at the panels again before reusing the verdicts")
}
areas$shows <- seen_by_eye$shows
areas$ground <- seen_by_eye$ground
by_ground <- function(g) areas$id[areas$ground == g]

# A Google Maps satellite link at a point inside each area. Google does not say
# when its image was taken, so it is an undated look at the ground, not a date.
ll <- crds(project(vect(cbind(areas$lab_x, areas$lab_y), crs = crs), "EPSG:4326"))
areas$google <- sprintf(
  "https://www.google.com/maps/@?api=1&map_action=map&center=%.5f,%.5f&zoom=17&basemap=satellite",
  ll[, 2], ll[, 1])

# Sentinel-2 brightening: each area's mean display value less the year before,
# less the same for the whole box, for every year. Forest is dark, so a patch
# opened to grass or bare ground brightens more than the box does that year.
s2_grey <- lapply(s2_view, mean)
box_mean <- vapply(s2_grey, function(r) global(r, "mean")[[1]], 1)
area_mean <- t(vapply(seq_len(nrow(areas)), function(a) {
  vapply(s2_grey, function(r) extract(r, area_v[a], fun = mean)[1, 2], 1)
}, numeric(length(years))))
rise <- t(apply(area_mean, 1, diff)) - matrix(diff(box_mean), nrow(areas), length(years) - 1,
                                              byrow = TRUE)
colnames(rise) <- years[-1]
areas$rise <- rise[cbind(seq_len(nrow(areas)), match(areas$year, years[-1]))]
areas$brightens <- areas$rise > 0
# the year of an area's largest rise against the box
areas$rise_year <- as.integer(colnames(rise)[apply(rise, 1, which.max)])

seen <- which(!is.na(areas$wb_before) & !is.na(areas$wb_after))
s2_only <- which(is.na(areas$wb_after) & !is.na(areas$wb_before))
# "in one summer": the mapped year's rise is more than twice any other year's;
# "over two summers": G rises in the year before its mapped year as well
one_summer <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(areas)), function(a) {
  r <- rise[a, ]
  k <- as.character(areas$year[a])
  r[[k]] > 2 * max(r[names(r) != k])
}, logical(1))
stopifnot(length(seen) + length(s2_only) == nrow(areas),
          setequal(c(by_ground("Change"), by_ground("Class error")), areas$id[seen]),
          setequal(c(by_ground("Likely change"), by_ground("Unclear")), areas$id[s2_only]),
          all(as.Date(areas$wb_before[s2_only]) == newest),
          all(one_summer[areas$id %in% c("F", "H", "I", "J")]), !one_summer[areas$id == "G"],
          with(list(r = rise[areas$id == "G", ]),
               min(r[c("2021", "2022")]) > 2 * max(abs(r[!names(r) %in% c("2021", "2022")]))),
          all(areas$rise_year[s2_only] == areas$year[s2_only]),
          areas$brightens[areas$id == "A"],
          all(areas$wb_before[seen] == areas$wb_before[seen[1]]),
          all(as.Date(areas$wb_after[seen]) == newest),
          all(areas$cutblock_share[areas$id != "I"] < 0.1),
          areas$cutblock_share[areas$id == "I"] >= 0.1,
          !is.na(areas$cutblock_year[areas$id == "I"]),
          names(which.max(box_mean)) == "2019")

# Colours: the floodplain edge from the gq registry's floodplain style, and one
# colour per change year; grey is change that never settled.
reg <- gq::gq_reg_main()
fp_col <- reg$layers$floodplains$fill$color
yr_set <- 2018:2023
yr_col <- setNames(hcl.colors(length(yr_set), "Plasma", rev = TRUE), yr_set)
grey_col <- grey(0.55)

draw_fp <- function(lwd = 1.5) {
  lines(fp_edge, col = "white", lwd = lwd + 1.5)
  lines(fp_edge, col = fp_col, lwd = lwd)
}
draw_area <- function(a, lwd = 1.5) {
  lines(area_v[a], col = "white", lwd = lwd + 1.5)
  lines(area_v[a], col = yr_col[as.character(areas$year[a])], lwd = lwd)
}
# white text on a dark band, so it reads over pale ground too
panel_label <- function(lab, right = FALSE, cex = 0.8) {
  u <- par("usr")
  pad <- 0.02 * (u[2] - u[1])
  x <- if (right) u[2] - 2 * pad else u[1] + 2 * pad
  y <- u[4] - 2 * pad
  w <- strwidth(lab, cex = cex, font = 2)
  h <- strheight(lab, cex = cex, font = 2)
  x0 <- if (right) x - w else x
  rect(x0 - pad, y - h - pad, x0 + w + pad, y + pad, col = adjustcolor("black", 0.45),
       border = NA)
  text(x0, y, lab, adj = c(0, 1), font = 2, col = "white", cex = cex)
}
view_ext <- function(a) {
  ext(unlist(areas[a, c("view_xmin", "view_xmax", "view_ymin", "view_ymax")]))
}
wb_view <- function(a, date) rast(d(paste0("wb_", areas$id[a], "_", date, ".tif")))

# One row of panels per area, each panel the area's view in one image, headed
# by a line with the area's Google Maps link so the two can be compared
area_rows <- function(rows, panels) {
  for (a in rows) {
    cat("\n\n**", areas$id[a], "** · ", areas$year[a], " · ", areas$from[a], " to ",
        areas$to[a], " · ", areas$ground[a], " · [Google Maps](", areas$google[a],
        "){target=\"_blank\"}\n\n", sep = "")
    op <- par(mfrow = c(1, length(panels)), mar = c(0.2, 0.2, 0.2, 0.2), bg = "white")
    for (k in seq_along(panels)) {
      plotRGB(panels[[k]]$img(a), scale = 255, mar = NA, axes = FALSE, ext = view_ext(a))
      draw_area(a)
      panel_label(panels[[k]]$label(a), right = TRUE, cex = 0.7)
      if (k == 1) panel_label(areas$id[a], cex = 1)
    }
    par(op)
  }
}
s2_panel <- function(offset) {
  list(img = function(a) s2_view[[as.character(areas$year[a] + offset)]],
       label = function(a) paste("Sentinel-2", areas$year[a] + offset))
}
wb_panel <- function(which) {
  list(img = function(a) wb_view(a, areas[[which]][a]),
       label = function(a) paste("Wayback", areas[[which]][a]))
}
```

drift finds where a floodplain's land cover changed, and dates it. This article
follows that change through one `r box_km[1]` × `r box_km[2]` km box of
floodplain in the Bulkley River watershed group, northern British Columbia,
where most of the change lies along Maxan Creek and Crow Creek. It then looks at each
change with drift's two imagery tools: sharp Esri Wayback images where they
exist, and a Sentinel-2 image of every summer. The sharp images say what
changed; here they stop in `r yr(newest)`, so the later changes are seen only
in Sentinel-2.

```{r fig-context, fig.height = 7 * nrow(relief) / ncol(relief), fig.cap = paste0("The box in the Bulkley River watershed group, northern British Columbia. Blue is the watershed group's floodplain and the darker line the Bulkley River; ground outside the group is dimmed, and the inset shows the group in the province. The scale bar is 20 km at the box's latitude. Basemap: ", relief_credit, ".")}
op <- par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0), bg = "white")
plotRGB(relief, scale = 255, mar = NA, axes = FALSE)
bulk_v <- ctx_v("bulk")
# outside the watershed group is dimmed
frame_v <- as.polygons(ext(relief), crs = crs(relief))
plot(erase(frame_v, bulk_v), add = TRUE, col = adjustcolor("white", 0.5), border = NA)
plot(ctx_v("floodplain"), add = TRUE, col = adjustcolor(fp_col, 0.75), border = NA)
lines(bulk_v, col = "grey20", lwd = 1.5)
river_v <- ctx_v("river")
lines(river_v, col = "#1F4E79", lwd = 1.2)
towns_v <- ctx_v("town")
points(towns_v, pch = 21, bg = "white", col = "grey10", cex = 0.8)
text(towns_v, ctx$name[ctx$part == "town"], pos = 4, offset = 0.4, cex = 0.75,
     col = "grey10", halo = TRUE, hc = "white")
# the river is labelled on its reach between Smithers and New Hazelton, clear of the
# study area
town_xy <- crds(towns_v)[ctx$name[ctx$part == "town"] %in% c("Smithers", "New Hazelton"), ]
river_pts <- crds(river_v)
near <- which.min(colSums((t(river_pts) - colMeans(town_xy))^2))
text(vect(river_pts[near, , drop = FALSE], crs = crs(relief)), "Bulkley River", font = 3,
     cex = 0.8, col = "#1F4E79", pos = 4, offset = 0.6, halo = TRUE, hc = "white")
# the box is a few pixels at this scale, so it is ringed as well
box_xy <- crds(centroids(ctx_v("box")))
points(box_xy, pch = 22, cex = 1.1, col = "red", bg = "red")
points(box_xy, pch = 1, cex = 3.5, col = "white", lwd = 4)
points(box_xy, pch = 1, cex = 3.5, col = "red", lwd = 2)
w <- xmax(relief) - xmin(relief)
text(vect(box_xy + c(-0.035, 0.02) * w, crs = crs(relief)), "Study area", adj = c(1, 0),
     font = 2, cex = 0.9, col = "red", halo = TRUE, hc = "white")
# Web Mercator stretches distance by 1 / cos(latitude)
k <- cos(mean(ext(project(ctx_v("box"), "EPSG:4326"))[3:4]) * pi / 180)
sbar(20000 / k, "topleft", type = "bar", divs = 2, below = "km", scaleby = 1000 / k,
     cex = 0.8)
legend("bottomleft", legend = c("Bulkley watershed group", "Floodplain", "Study area"),
       col = c("grey20", adjustcolor(fp_col, 0.75), "red"), lwd = c(1.5, NA, NA),
       pch = c(NA, 15, 22), pt.bg = c(NA, NA, "red"), pt.cex = c(NA, 1.8, 1.1),
       bg = "white", cex = 0.8, inset = 0.02)
# BC inset
par(fig = c(0.74, 0.98, 0.74, 0.98), new = TRUE, mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
bc_v <- ctx_v("bc")
plot(bc_v, col = "grey92", border = "grey45", axes = FALSE, mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0),
     background = "white", box = TRUE)
plot(ctx_v("bulk_bc"), add = TRUE, col = "red", border = NA)
par(op)
```

drift finds `r nrow(areas)` change areas in the box, lettered `r areas$id[1]` to
`r areas$id[nrow(areas)]` on the map in the next section: patches of 1 ha or more
where neighbouring floodplain cells switched land cover in the same year and
stayed. Sharp images from before and after reach `r length(seen)` of them, and show only `r paste(by_ground("Change"), collapse = ", ")` as a change:
`r paste(by_ground("Class error"), collapse = ", ")` are class errors, where the
land-cover map gave the same ground a different class. The
`r length(c(by_ground("Likely change"), by_ground("Unclear")))` areas dated after
`r yr(newest)` have no sharp image after their change, only Sentinel-2:
`r paste(by_ground("Likely change"), collapse = ", ")` look like forest opening up,
and `r paste(by_ground("Unclear"), collapse = ", ")` is unclear.

## What changed in this floodplain, and when?

The floodplain and its land cover are a published STAC item, `r item$item`
(processed `r substr(item$processed, 1, 10)` with drift `r item$drift` and flooded
`r item$flooded`): the floodplain polygon, and Impact Observatory's 10 m land
cover for every year from 2017 to 2023, clipped to it. `dft_rast_break_class()`
reads the seven years in each cell and finds the year its class switched, and
`dft_rast_break_category()` says whether the switch held.

```{r fetch-landcover, eval = FALSE, code = c(from_script("aoi"), "", from_script("stac-item"), "", from_script("floodplain"), "", from_script("landcover"), "", from_script("dates"))}
```

The figures below read the small files that script saved, so the page itself
makes no network call.

```{r read-saved, ref.label = "data", eval = FALSE}
```

```{r fig-lead, fig.height = 7 * asp, fig.cap = paste0("Floodplain cells by the year their land cover switched and stayed switched, over the ", years[length(years)], " Sentinel-2 image. Grey cells changed but never settled on one class. Uncoloured floodplain cells either kept their class or flickered and came back to it. Ground outside the floodplain is dimmed. Letters name the change areas of 1 ha or more. The blue line is the edge of the floodplain; the scale bar is 500 m.")}
op <- par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0), bg = "white")
plotRGB(s2_view[[length(s2_view)]], scale = 255, mar = NA, axes = FALSE)
plot(outside, add = TRUE, col = "white", alpha = 0.45, legend = FALSE, axes = FALSE)
# change.tif stores a switch year less 2000, 1 for never settled, 0 and 2 for
# no lasting change, and NA outside the floodplain
yr_layer <- classify(change, rbind(c(0, NA), c(2, NA)))
coltab(yr_layer) <- data.frame(value = c(1, yr_set - 2000), col = c(grey_col, yr_col))
plot(yr_layer, add = TRUE, legend = FALSE, axes = FALSE, alpha = 0.85)
draw_fp(1.2)
text(vect(cbind(areas$lab_x, areas$lab_y), crs = crs), areas$id,
     col = "black", font = 2, cex = 0.8, halo = TRUE, hc = "white")
sbar(500, "topleft", type = "bar", divs = 2, below = "", label = "", col = "white")
legend("bottomright", legend = c(yr_set, "never settled"), fill = c(yr_col, grey_col),
       border = NA, bg = "white", cex = 0.75, ncol = 2, inset = 0.02)
par(op)
```

Grey is change that never settled, and this article sets it aside, along with
the cells that flickered and came back. The coloured cells switched once and stayed, which gives each a date. A
date from a 10 m map is a place to look, though, not yet a change on the
ground, so each lettered area is looked at below.

## What does drift give us to look with?

```{r tools, echo = FALSE}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Tool = c("`dft_rast_break_class()`, `dft_rast_break_category()`",
           "`dft_stac_composite()`",
           "`dft_wayback_captures()`, `dft_wayback_pick()`, `dft_wayback_fetch()`"),
  `What it gives` = c("The year each cell's land cover switched, and whether it held",
                      "A Sentinel-2 image of every summer, at 10 m",
                      "Sharp (under 1 m) images where Esri holds them, but only from the days its providers imaged the place"),
  check.names = FALSE
), caption = "drift's tools for dating change and looking at it.")
```

`dft_stac_composite()` reads Sentinel-2 from Microsoft's Planetary Computer.
For each summer it takes the June and July scenes with under 20% cloud, masks
cloud and snow, and
keeps the median of each band. The panels share one display stretch, so a
difference in brightness between them is in the data, not the display. A
composite can still carry pale patches: the 2019 image is the palest of the
seven.

```{r fetch-composites, eval = FALSE, code = from_script("composites")}
```

Esri Wayback keeps the versions of Esri's World Imagery basemap released since
2014. Each
version, a *release*, is a mosaic of images taken on many days, so drift reads
which *capture* (the day an image was taken) each release draws over the box,
then picks and fetches by capture.

```{r fetch-wayback, eval = FALSE, code = c(from_script("wayback"), "", from_script("wayback-fetch"))}
```

## What do the sharp images show?

For the `r length(seen)` areas dated `r min(areas$year[seen])` to
`r max(areas$year[seen])`, Wayback has a sharp image from before the change
(`r fmt(areas$wb_before[seen[1]])`) and one from `r fmt(newest)`, after the change
or, for the areas dated `r yr(newest)`, late in its year.

Each row below is one area: Wayback before the change and at its end or after
it, then Sentinel-2 the summer before and the summer of the change. The outline
is the area, in the colour of its year, and the link above each row opens
Google's satellite image of it, which Google does not date.

```{r fig-seen, results = "asis", fig.height = 7 / 4}
area_rows(seen, list(wb_panel("wb_before"), wb_panel("wb_after"), s2_panel(-1), s2_panel(0)))
```

Only C is a change on the ground. The forest along Maxan Creek has opened up by
`r yr(newest)`. A, D and E are parts of one open meadow, which the land-cover
map moved from Crops to Rangeland; where it was mown in 2016, across D and parts
of A and E, it is grassed over by `r yr(newest)`, a change of use at most. B is the same stand of trees in both.
Sentinel-2 alone would not have shown this: in its year A brightens more than the
box as a whole does, just as a cleared patch would.

## What changed after `r yr(newest)`?

For the `r length(s2_only)` areas dated `r min(areas$year[s2_only])` to
`r max(areas$year[s2_only])`, the last sharp image is the one from
`r fmt(newest)`. It shows F, H, I and J as forest, and G as an open wet meadow
along a channel.

Each row is one area: the last sharp Wayback image (`r fmt(newest)`), then
Sentinel-2 the summer before and the summer of the change.

```{r fig-s2only, results = "asis", fig.height = 7 / 3}
area_rows(s2_only, list(wb_panel("wb_before"), s2_panel(-1), s2_panel(0)))
```

Of the six years, each area brightens most, against the box as a whole, in the
year the map gives it. For F, H, I and J that is forest opening up in one summer,
which bears the date out. G brightens over two
summers and was already open in `r yr(newest)`, so the map's switch from Trees
there may be a label catching up with what was on the ground. Part of I
lies in a cutblock the province records as harvested from
`r areas$cutblock_year[areas$id == "I"]`, and none of the others lies mostly in
one. What happened in F, G, H and J cannot be told at 10 m: a cut, a slide and
a channel moving would all look alike.

## Why do the sharp images stop in `r yr(newest)`?

Wayback can show only what Esri's providers imaged and Esri released. Over this
box, the releases from 2015 on draw `r nrow(sharp)` sharp captures at the zoom
levels read (16 to 18), from `r paste(fmt(sharp$capture_date), collapse = ", ")`.
The newest is still the one drawn by every release from `r fmt(newest_first)` to
`r fmt(newest_last)`, the latest. Nothing newer has been released here, so a change after `r yr(newest)` has no sharp image yet. Sentinel-2 images
every summer, but at 10 m.

## The numbers

```{r numbers, echo = FALSE}
fp_ha <- function(w) round(summ$ha[summ$what == w], 1)
ord <- order(match(areas$ground, c("Class error", "Change", "Likely change", "Unclear")),
             areas$year, areas$id)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Area = areas$id, Year = areas$year,
  `Land cover` = paste(areas$from, "to", areas$to),
  `On the ground` = areas$ground,
  `What the imagery shows` = areas$shows,
  ha = areas$ha,
  Cutblock = ifelse(areas$cutblock_share >= 0.1,
                    paste0(round(100 * areas$cutblock_share), "% in a ", areas$cutblock_year, " block"), ""),
  check.names = FALSE
)[ord, ], row.names = FALSE, caption = paste0("The change areas, class errors first. On the ground is what the imagery shows: a change or a class error where Wayback has sharp images from before and after, and a likely change or unclear where only Sentinel-2 does. Cutblock is the share of the area inside a BC consolidated cutblock, with the block's harvest start year, where that is 10% or more. Across the box, the floodplain's 10 m cells hold ",
  fp_ha("Stable"), " ha with no change, ", fp_ha("Changed once, and stayed"), " ha that switched once and stayed, ",
  fp_ha("Changed, never settled"), " ha that changed and never settled, and ", fp_ha("Flickered and came back"),
  " ha that flickered and came back to its first class."))
```

## Limits

- A clean switch is a date to look at, not a confirmed change: the land-cover
  map moves unchanged ground between similar classes, as it moved one meadow
  here from Crops to Rangeland.
- A switch in 2018 or 2023 rests on a single year of land cover on one side of it.
- Wayback shows only what Esri has released, and here nothing after
  `r fmt(newest)`; the `r fmt(sharp$capture_date[sharp$cover_max < 0.99])` capture covers only part
  of the box.
- Sentinel-2 at 10 m shows the year ground brightened. Where forest opened up,
  that bears out the map's date, but a meadow brightens in years its cover did
  not change, as A, D and E do. It cannot say what happened, and a composite can
  carry pale patches.
